Tables: interactive, filterable and pivot tables

Source: vignettes/tables.Rmd
tables.Rmd

rvis table wrappers show a data frame as an interactive html table: sortable and searchable (DT), filterable and editable with cell graphics (TFD3, D3TableFilter), or reshaped by the reader (pivot). Examples are evaluated when the package of the wrapper is installed; otherwise only their code is shown.

Data: violent crime rates by US state (USArrests)

USArrests gives arrests per 100,000 residents for assault, murder and rape in each US state in 1973, and the percent of the population living in urban areas. state.region adds the region of each state.

arrests <- data.frame(USArrests, region = as.character(state.region))
head(arrests)
#>            Murder Assault UrbanPop Rape region
#> Alabama      13.2     236       58 21.2  South
#> Alaska       10.0     263       48 44.5   West
#> Arizona       8.1     294       80 31.0   West
#> Arkansas      8.8     190       50 19.5  South
#> California    9.0     276       91 40.6   West
#> Colorado      7.9     204       78 38.7   West

Tables

The label dimension selects the columns to show (all columns by default). Row names are shown when config$withRowNames is TRUE.

DT 

rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "DT", obj = arrests,
         config = list(paging.length = 5))

TFD3 (embedded in rvis)

TFD3 tables have a filter row (try >10 in the Murder column) and can turn cells into graphics with config$column.shape and colour columns with config$column.color.

rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "TFD3", obj = arrests,
         label = list("Murder", "Assault", "UrbanPop", "region"),
         config = list(column.shape = list(Assault = "bar"),
                       column.color = list(UrbanPop = c("white", "steelblue")),
                       column.footer = list(Murder = mean, Assault = mean),
                       height = 400))

D3TableFilter

D3TableFilter is the published version of the TFD3 widget and takes the same settings.

rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "D3TableFilter", obj = arrests,
         config = list(column.shape = list(Murder = "bubble")))

Tables from a long table

TFD3 

rvisPlot(type = "table.molten", plotter = "TFD3", obj = arrests, label = list("region", "Murder", "Assault"))

Pivot tables

A pivot table lets the reader drag columns into rows and columns and choose how values are aggregated and shown (table, heat map, charts).

pivot 

rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "pivot", obj = arrests, rows = "region",
         vals = "Murder", aggregatorName = "Average", rendererName = "Heatmap")

Legacy table function

DT.Table() is an older function kept for backward compatibility: it takes the table as x and DataTables options directly.

DT.Table(arrests, options = list(pageLength = 5))
